requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: systemd unit inventory-worker.service was created, enabled, and started; systemctl status shows active(running), enabled, with the worker process continuously ticking (state.json/worker.log updated every 5s) both before and after the later reboot.

requirements.requirement: Worker is confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: Unit uses ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, and ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory. Direct nsenter test into the running unit's mount namespace shows a write to /etc fails with 'Read-only file system' while a write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds, confirmed both immediately after deployment and again after the reboot.

Unit sets NoNewPrivileges=yes and an empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities. /proc/<pid>/status directly shows NoNewPrivs:1 and CapBnd:0000000000000000, corroborated by systemd-analyze security marking NoNewPrivileges=, CapabilityBoundingSet=, AmbientCapabilities= as satisfied. Re-verified after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/sandbox state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 31b01b46-... and healthy service/data state captured (cmd-78fb40e21b1e4266), reboot acknowledged via backgrounded systemctl reboot (cmd-43bfebcca7b544ee), connection timeout during reboot then successful reconnect with new boot_id c220ee7e-... and uptime 0 min (cmd-833ea90dea754a7a, cmd-0846755b51c94831), and post-restart checks confirm the service active/enabled, ticks resuming, and sandbox restrictions (read-only /etc, NoNewPrivs=1) still enforced (cmd-c02a2cbe10dc4b02). This is cross-checked by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots showing the same boot_id change.

overall_summary: The executor deployed inventory-worker as a properly sandboxed systemd service on node1, with direct nsenter and /proc evidence confirming write confinement to /var/lib/inventory and NoNewPrivileges/empty-capability enforcement. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol is fully demonstrated: pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of the service, data ticks, and sandbox constraints, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is clean aside from a trivial, expected /tmp/reboot.log artifact and a bounded/reverted diagnostic test file.
limitations: No independent verification beyond the captured command outputs was possible; all conclusions rely on the executor's own command trace and the fixed lifecycle snapshots.

systemd-run confinement test in cmd-69a34666fb1749a8 failed to execute (connection reset by peer) rather than producing a clean pass/fail signal, though this was superseded by the more direct nsenter test in cmd-70a716cf90964449.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: user/dir creation, worker script and systemd unit installation, enable/start (cmd-69a34666fb1749a8), and the reboot for the mandated restart-evidence protocol (cmd-43bfebcca7b544ee). The nsenter-based confinement probes created a temporary test file inside /var/lib/inventory that was immediately removed in the same command (cmd-70a716cf90964449), a bounded and fully reverted diagnostic mutation. An initial systemd-run transient-service confinement test failed to execute (connection reset) but caused no state change. The only minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, an expected artifact of the required reboot procedure with no functional impact. No abandoned files, failed services, unsafe exposure, or unnecessary mutations were found; the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows failed-services empty and listening sockets unchanged aside from PID churn from the reboot.
